newsitem.title: USA: Vivus reports surprisingly strong first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Vivus reports surprisingly strong first quarter.

text.p: Vivus Inc. Tuesday reported that first quarter profits more than doubled Wall Street estimates, reflecting robust sales of its new MUSE treatment for male impotence.

The Menlo Park, Calif.-based company reported earnings of $9.6 million, or 54 cents a share, for the quarter, vs. a loss of $6.2 million, or 45 cents a share, in the year-ago period. First-quarter sales totaled $27.8 million.
Industry analysts on average predicted earnings of 20 cents a share, according to the First Call service, which tracks such forecasts.
The earnings report was the first solid indication of the demand for MUSE -- the Medicated Urethral System for Erection -- whose launch earlier this year sent Vivus's stock soaring.
More recently, however, Vivus shares have been among the most volatile on the market, losing half their value amid concern that enthusiasm for MUSE had been overstated.

MUSE is an ultrathin applicator containing a medication that impotent men can insert into the tip of their penises to produce an erection within about 10 minutes. It has been hailed as a dramatic improvement over traditional treatments that required injecting the drug with a needle, or surgically implanting balloons that can be inflated with a pump.
Before the earnings report, estimates of actual market size were highly speculative, and investors were eager for a more solid indication of demand.

Vivus shares, which rose $3.375 to $41.375 Tuesday in anticipation of the earnings report, rose another $3 in after-hours trading shortly after the first-quarter results were released. But the stock remained well below its high for the year of $81.25.
Vivus said demand continued to exceed its current production capacity and it is building a new factory in New Jersey. The company is evaluating additional manufacturing sites in Europe.
